literal: Public gossip to feel ashamed is it possible, 'Do not fear, guard yourself' he said, many people to feel ashamed when he abandoned?
translation: When he, who once assured me 'Do not fear,' has abandoned me so heartlessly that even onlookers feel ashamed, is it possible for me to feel ashamed of this public gossip?
modern: "அஞ்சாதே, உன்னைப் பாதுகாப்பேன்" என்று அன்று சொன்னவர், இன்று பலர் வெட்கப்படும்படியாக என்னை விட்டுப் பிரிந்து சென்ற பிறகு, இந்த ஊர் அலருக்கு (வதந்திக்கு) நான் அஞ்சுவது இயலுமா?
explanation: The heroine laments her lover's departure. He had once comforted her with the words 'añcal ōmpu' (do not fear, guard yourself), promising never to leave her. Now, he has abandoned her so publicly and cruelly that even the townspeople ('palar') feel ashamed on her behalf. In such a desperate state of public abandonment, she asks if it is even possible ('olvatō') for her to feel embarrassed or shrink back in shame ('nāṇa') because of the town's gossip ('alar'). The gossip is nothing compared to the profound betrayal of his broken promise.
